properties.description:
`GraphRead` (crates/reflow2-core/src/graph_read.rs) — the Rust trait realizing `ifc:graph-read`, and the second trait ever to exist in this crate. `LlmBackend` was the first and the only, since 2026-07.

`impl GraphRead for DesignGraph` delegates to the inherent methods and hides nothing, so the 274-function struct is untouched and every existing caller keeps working. What it adds is the option to ask for `&dyn GraphRead` instead.

THE PILOT IS `granularity`. Its body moved out of `impl DesignGraph` into a free `granularity_report(g: &dyn GraphRead)`, with a one-line inherent method left behind so `report.rs`, `ility.rs` and the existing tests never noticed. A refactor that forced its callers to change would be paying for the boundary twice.

WHAT THE MOVE BUYS, demonstrated rather than asserted, in three tests:
  — RUNS WITH NO STORE. The same report computed over a design that is two Vec's: no RocksDB, no schema, no disk, no lock.
  — CANNOT TELL WHICH IMPLEMENTATION IT IS READING. Population, mean and the flagged artifact ids are asserted EQUAL between a real DesignGraph and a hand-built fake sharing no code with it. Had the module reached past the contract for anything at all, this would not compile, let alone agree.
  — LETS A REFUSAL THROUGH. An unknown node type arrives as an error, not as an empty design — with a control case proving an empty-but-valid design is `Ok`, so the assertion is not vacuous.

AND THE COMPILER NOW ENFORCES WHAT THE DOCS ASSERTED: `GraphRead` has no writes, so a module behind it cannot change what it reads.

NOT YET DONE, and deliberately not overstated: 15 other read-only modules are recorded as consuming this contract but still take `&self` on DesignGraph. This is one module, proven end to end, so the cost of the next is known rather than guessed.
properties.name: A module stands behind the read contract, so it can be swapped, tested with no store, and held still to be measured
